evaluation_label: post-test regression evaluation; not a new independent test
revision_note: Six deterministic fault-injection tests were added on 24 August 2026 and all passed: low-disk event-video degradation, camera reconnect, video-timestamp fallback, model-class-order startup rejection, failed-manifest retention, and event-buffer pre/post duration. The tests use synthetic inputs and mocks only and do not change detector code, weights, thresholds, original outputs, or reported evaluation results. The earlier 24 August addition of the retrospective Final candidate v1 review remains authoritative: 12 TP, 5 FP, 70.6% precision, and 6/7 event coverage.

superseded_automatic_matching_results.status: retained for audit history; not authoritative for final thesis reporting

portability_revision.scope: packaging and runtime path resolution only

clean_copy_full_video_smoke_test.scope: engineering reproducibility only; not an independent generalisation test

fault_injection_tests.scope: synthetic fault injection only; no participant video and no detector inference

tests.name: Low-disk-space degradation
tests.evidence: Event-video creation was disabled while the monitoring path remained callable.

tests.name: Camera disconnect and recovery
tests.evidence: Two failed reads triggered reopen; a frame from the replacement capture was delivered.

tests.name: Video timestamp fallback
tests.evidence: Non-increasing/negative timestamps resolved to monotonic frame-time values [0.0, 0.1, 0.2].

tests.name: Weight class-order startup rejection
tests.evidence: A deliberately reordered phone model class map raised RuntimeError before monitoring began.

tests.name: Manifest failure-state retention
tests.evidence: Both latest and timestamped manifests retained failed status, exception, and finish time.

tests.name: Event-buffer pre/post duration
tests.evidence: At 10 FPS the clip retained frames 10-40: 1.0 s pre-trigger plus 2.0 s post-trigger.
